prompt: What does Import V3 change about how bulk import works compared with Import V2, and why was it needed? Is it what runs by default now?
key: Written in docs/design-docs/design_docs/20260921-import-v3-reshard-design.md (created 2026-09-21, implemented in #53334 on 2026-10-19). Import V2 reads every source file twice (PreImportTask keeps only statistics, ImportTaskV2 reads it again), hashes rows per file-group and writes into pre-allocated segments, so each (vchannel, partition) bucket is split by every file-group task: many small segments, and a hashed_stats table growing with V × P that can exceed etcd's 1.5 MiB request size. V3 parses each source once in a ReshardTask: normalized, routed to its bucket, sorted and written as immutable fragments; Planning packs fragments into per-segment, bucket-local plans across all sources, and each ImportTaskV3 k-way merges one plan into exactly one sorted segment, so the post-import Sorting compaction is skipped. It also fails loudly on a mid-import schema change instead of hanging in IndexBuilding as V2 can. Ordinary imports first run a count-only preimport and get exact per-file ID ranges (AssigningIDRange). It is not the default: it sits behind the one-way dataCoord.import.enableImportV3 gate, default false, to be enabled only once every DataNode and DataCoord supports it and not disabled again; L0 import stays on Import V2.
